answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules, the November guide establishes that schedules create or attach to subscriptions, sequence phases, and update subscriptions as phases start (new 9-23, 45-47). It conditions the draft first invoice and approximate one-hour finalization on a schedule-created charge_automatically subscription, with later open or paid dependent on asynchronous payment outcome (new 231-237). It adds automatic_tax to the inheritable schedule/phase fields and warns that manual tax rates cannot coexist with automatic tax in one phase (new 118-141). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-schedules]] matches older core material but retains a May classic-editor-only limit and overstates the draft invoice, four-field inheritance and direct auto-split claims (source 13/19/36/50; old 8, 223-229, 551-561). Accounts v2 customer_account versus Customer v1 customer remain distinct, with preview qualification at new 241-275.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules, substantive changes include Dashboard workflows without the May classic-only sentence, fifth automatic_tax inheritance with non-fallback tax rules, finite Dashboard end-date cancellation versus API release, backdate access control, and state-specific release/cancel consequences (new 17, 118-141, 522-588, 833-859; old 8, 119-133, 639-641, 958-974). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-schedules]] should date the May UI limit, qualify first-invoice draft timing at source 19, expand inheritance at 36, and change categorical auto-splitting at 50 to 'might' except the item-delete example. The old Node.js to new curl/Ruby sample change and Markdown numbering are presentation, not API deprecation (old 243-295; new 249-275). Schedule update omissions unset prior settings (new 318), release before start creates no subscription (new 835), and draft/open/paid invoice statuses do not establish actual payment or settlement.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/billing-credits, the new capture documents customer Credit Grants for prepaid or promotional merchant offerings and a meter-event to meter/price to invoice flow (new 7-23, 41-43). Grant use on an invoice depends on period_end versus effective_at/expires_at, balance at finalization, matching currency, and metered-price subscription items reporting through Meters; one-off, licensed, one-time setup and legacy Usage Records lines are excluded (new 53-69; old 45-61). Credits apply after discounts, before taxes and invoice_credit_balance, and only settle onto an invoice at finalization (new 71-101; old 63-93). [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-credits-overview]] preserves most rules, but its prohibited-use phrase at line 19 is narrower than both captures' approved merchant products/services list (new 29-39; old 21-31). A preview is not final credit application or paid-invoice evidence.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/billing-credits, the old Public preview banner (old 6) is absent from the new capture (new 5-7), but this does not establish GA or account eligibility. The new text diagram (new 14-23; old 15 unavailable), link additions, heading style and typography are presentational. Eligibility, five-step grant priority, finalization-only consumption, 100 unused-grant ledger-balance limit, and void-versus-Credit Note behavior are stable (new 53-145; old 45-137). [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-credits-overview]] should date its preview statement and correct its 'non-subscription spending' prohibition: both old 24,29 and new 32,37 allow memberships, pay-as-you-go plans and specific merchant goods/services while barring stored value outside those categories. The related concept already routes the source; no grant application, payment success or refund is demonstrated.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/how-it-works, the new capture explicitly scopes this page to basic Billing Meters usage billing and recommends Metronome for new integrations unless maintaining an existing Meter integration (new 9-24). For the basic path, customer activity produces meter events; meters aggregate usage, prices rate it, subscriptions link the customer and prices, and invoices are generated in a four-component ingestion/catalog/billing/monitoring lifecycle (new 26-49; old 8-20). Customer-configured Accounts or Customers represent the billing identity; meter events have a customer identifier and optional timestamp/idempotency/dimensions; Meter Event Summaries update asynchronously (new 57-70; old 28-42). [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-how-it-works]] currently summarizes the older basic Meter path but omits the new recommendation; none of the examples proves successful billing or payment.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/how-it-works, the substantive addition is the Metronome-versus-basic selection guidance and comparative claims about real-time tracking, invoice-time credit reconciliation, enterprise contracts and dimensional pricing (new 9-24; absent old 4-19). [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-how-it-works]] should date its older 'new v2 approach' framing and label its lifecycle and six definitions as basic Billing Meters, while the related concept's 'current approach' phrase receives a reciprocal qualification (new 11,24; old 8-42). The four steps and six definitions are retained (new 26-70; old 8-42); text diagram and See also link are presentation/navigation additions (new 39-49,72-74; old 19-20). The claim about no live mid-cycle totals must be read with asynchronously available custom-period summaries (new 17,70; old 42). This capture does not prove Meter deprecation, Metronome eligibility, an invoice or a payment result.
